newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian-Russian oil venture raises share capital.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian-Russian oil venture raises share capital.

text.p: Bulgarian-Russian oil joint venture Rosbulneft has decided to raise its share capital to two billion levs from 50 million levs, officials said on Tuesday.

"Our shareholders meeting decided on Monday in Bourgas to raise the venture's share capital to two billion levs aiming at financial stability," Rosneft's president Alexander Putilov told a news conference.
"We plan further big increases of the venture's capital in the nearest future," he said.
Rosbulneft, a venture between Russian state-owned oil company Rosneft and Bulgaria's biggest refinery Neftohim at the Black Sea port of Bourgas, was established last October.
It supplies Neftohim with crude, and sells the products to suppliers for the Bulgarian market.
Putilov said the two companies continued to hold equal shares after the venture's capital increase.
He said the shareholders meeting had also discussed the venture's short and long-term business programme.
"We looked at alternatives for the financial stabilisation of Rosbulneft as the unstable national currency (the lev) creates problems on the (local) petrol products market," Putilov said.
Putilov said the shareholders meeting had decided to expand into direct sales of their own production and would focus on building filling stations and on direct sales to big industrial consumers.
He said the sites for the first two filling stations in Bourgas had already been chosen.
"We will build several petrol stations in Sofia and thus we will get into the country's biggest market of petrol products," Putilov said.
Putilov declined to say what Rosbulneft's profits would be this year but said they all would be reinvested to develop the venture's activities.
Rosneft export director Valentin Zlatev said Rosbulneft would supply up to five million tonnes of crude to Neftohim this year at preferential prices.
"Our average monthly supplies are 4-5 oil tankers and each of them carries some 70,000 tonnes of crude," Zlatev said, adding that Rosbulneft supplied almost half of Neftohim's oil each month.
He said Rosbulneft would supply four oil tankers to Neftohim this month.
Zlatev denied newspaper reports that Neftohim had debt outstanding to Rosbulneft but said they sometimes delayed their payments from 20 to 40 days as they had difficulties getting dollars.
